data: Antares pad for Cygnus ISS cargo (2013-2023) and the Minotaur V launch of the LADEE Moon probe

Launch Pad 0 is the launch complex of the Mid-Atlantic Regional Spaceport (MARS) at the southern tip of Wallops Island, Virginia, owned and operated by the Virginia Spaceport Authority next to NASA's Wallops Flight Facility. Pad 0A was built for the Conestoga rocket, whose single flight on 23 October 1995 self-destructed at T+46 seconds, and was rebuilt for Antares, which flew 18 times from it between 21 April 2013 and 2 August 2023. Pad 0B launched its first Minotaur I in December 2006 and the Minotaur V with LADEE on 7 September 2013. Sources: Wikipedia (MARS, Antares, Conestoga, LADEE), Virginia Spaceport Authority, NASASpaceflight; coordinates from Wikipedia.
Antares 230 launches Cygnus OA-5 from Wallops — NASASpaceflight

Pad 0 is the launch complex at the southern tip of Wallops Island, Virginia, owned by the Virginia Spaceport Authority beside NASA's Wallops Flight Facility. Pad 0A was built for the Conestoga rocket, which flew once, on 23 October 1995, and self-destructed 46 seconds after liftoff. It was rebuilt for Antares, which launched from it 18 times between 21 April 2013 and 2 August 2023, mostly Cygnus cargo ships bound for the International Space Station: 17 successes and one failure, Orb-3 on 28 October 2014. The pad reopened with Cygnus OA-5 on 17 October 2016, and since August 2023 has been rebuilt for the Antares 330. Pad 0B, a few hundred metres to the south-west, has launched Minotaur rockets, most recently in June 2021. Its Minotaur V sent LADEE to the Moon on 7 September 2013, so far the only mission to another celestial body launched from Wallops. Launch azimuths of 38 to 60 degrees suit station orbits.
